title: Penalty and compensation for damage to computer, computer system, etc.
issuing_authority: Parliament of India
summary: Imposes civil liability and compensation (up to Rs. 5 crore adjudication) for unauthorized access, downloading or copying data, introducing computer contaminants/viruses, damaging or disrupting computer systems, denying access to authorized users, or facilitating unauthorized access.
practical_application: Used to claim statutory financial compensation before the State Cyber Adjudicating Officer (IT Secretary of State) from hackers, rogue apps, or negligent institutions when funds or confidential data are extracted.

title: Computer related offences
issuing_authority: Parliament of India
summary: Criminalizes any act referred to in Section 43 if done dishonestly or fraudulently. Punishable with imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine up to 5 lakh rupees, or both.
practical_application: Applied in FIRs when cybercriminals breach net banking portals, email accounts, or digital wallets with fraudulent intent.

title: Punishment for identity theft
issuing_authority: Parliament of India
summary: Whoever, fraudulently or dishonestly make use of the electronic signature, password or any other unique identification feature of any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to 1 lakh rupees.
practical_application: Crucial provision invoked for SIM swap fraud, interception or theft of OTPs, stealing UPI MPIN, ATM cloning, and using another person's login credentials to authorize payments.

title: Punishment for cheating by personation by using computer resource
issuing_authority: Parliament of India
summary: Whoever, by means of any computer resource or communication device cheats by personating, shall be punished with imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to 1 lakh rupees.
practical_application: The most widely applied cyber section in India for phishing calls, fake customer care executive numbers on Google Search, AnyDesk/TeamViewer remote screen-sharing scams, and fake lottery/task fraud.

title: Punishment for violation of privacy
issuing_authority: Parliament of India
summary: Capturing, publishing or transmitting the image of a private area of any person without consent. Imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to 2 lakh rupees or both.
practical_application: Applied directly against illegal loan app recovery agents who morph victim photos accessed from contact lists to blackmail or extort money.

title: Cheating (Replacing Section 415 & 420 IPC)
issuing_authority: Parliament of India
jurisdiction: All India (for offences on or after July 1, 2024)
summary: Dishonestly inducing any person to deliver property or make/alter valuable securities. Section 318(4) provides imprisonment up to 7 years and fine for cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property.
practical_application: Mandatory primary criminal charge for all financial scams, online fraud schemes, fake telegram investments, and deceptive inducement to transfer money.

title: Cheating by Personation (Replacing Section 416 & 419 IPC)
issuing_authority: Parliament of India
jurisdiction: All India (for offences on or after July 1, 2024)
summary: Cheating by pretending to be some other person, or by knowingly substituting one person for another, or representing that he or any other person is a person other than he or such other person really is. Imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine, or both.
practical_application: Applied when fraudsters pose as Police officers, CBI, ED, Customs, or RBI officials in 'Digital Arrest' extortion scams.

title: Criminal Breach of Trust (Replacing Section 405 & 406 IPC)
issuing_authority: Parliament of India
jurisdiction: All India (for offences on or after July 1, 2024)
summary: Whoever, being entrusted with property or dominion over property, dishonestly misappropriates or converts to own use that property. Imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine, or both.
practical_application: Applied against fintech apps, rogue payment gateways, or merchant aggregators that receive customer funds and refuse to refund or credit the recipient.

title: Forgery and Using Forged Electronic Records (Replacing Sections 463, 468, 471 IPC)
issuing_authority: Parliament of India
jurisdiction: All India (for offences on or after July 1, 2024)
summary: Making false documents or electronic records with intent to cause damage or commit fraud, and fraudulently using such forged records as genuine.
practical_application: Applied when scammers generate fake bank payment receipts, fraudulent court orders, or fake arrest warrants on WhatsApp.

title: Information in cognizable cases (Zero FIR & e-FIR) (Replacing Section 154 CrPC)
issuing_authority: Parliament of India
summary: Mandates that every police station must register information relating to a cognizable offence irrespective of territorial jurisdiction (Zero FIR). Allows electronic communication of information (e-FIR) to be signed within 3 days.
practical_application: Protects victims when local police stations try to reject cybercrime complaints claiming 'the bank branch is elsewhere' or 'the scammer is in another state'.

act: Reserve Bank of India Master Circular
title: Customer Protection – Limiting Liability of Customers in Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions
issuing_authority: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
jurisdiction: All Commercial Banks, Small Finance Banks, Payments Banks in India
summary:
Fundamental regulation governing unauthorized digital banking transactions:
1. Zero Liability of Customer: (a) Contributory fraud/negligence/deficiency on the part of the bank (irrespective of whether reported or not); (b) Third party breach where deficiency lies neither with bank nor customer but elsewhere in the system, AND customer notifies the bank within THREE (3) working days of receiving SMS/email alert.
2. Limited Liability: If customer reports between 4 to 7 working days, liability is capped: Basic Savings Bank Deposit (BSBD) accounts: Max ₹5,000; Other Savings/Overdraft/Cards with limit up to ₹5 lakh: Max ₹10,000; Accounts/Cards with limit above ₹5 lakh: Max ₹25,000.
3. Beyond 7 working days: Determined as per bank board-approved policy.
4. Burden of Proof: Paragraph 12 explicitly mandates that the burden of proving customer liability lies ON THE BANK.
5. Reversal Timeline: Bank must credit the unauthorized amount to customer account within 10 working days of reporting (shadow reversal), subject to resolution within 90 days.
practical_application: The master legal shield for banking fraud victims in India. If a customer reports within 3 days without sharing credentials, the bank is legally obligated to credit the money back. The bank cannot simply reject a claim without proving customer negligence.

title: Grounds of Complaint and Award by Ombudsman
issuing_authority: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
jurisdiction: All RBI Regulated Entities (Banks, NBFCs, System Participants)
summary: Establishes a cost-free dispute resolution mechanism. Customer can file a complaint on CMS portal (cms.rbi.org.in) if the bank rejects the complaint, fails to reply within 30 days, or provides an unsatisfactory resolution. The Ombudsman can award compensation up to ₹30 lakh for consequential loss, plus up to ₹1 lakh for loss of time, expenses, and mental harassment.
practical_application: The second-tier recourse when a bank refuses to refund unauthorized electronic transactions or dismisses an RBI Zero Liability dispute.

title: Obligations of Data Fiduciary & Data Breach Reporting
issuing_authority: Parliament of India
summary: Mandates that Data Fiduciaries (including banks, payment aggregators, fintech apps) implement reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breaches. Mandates intimation of breaches to the Data Protection Board of India and affected individuals.
practical_application: Invoked when unauthorized transactions stem from corporate data leaks, compromised bank databases, or third-party fintech API vulnerabilities.

title: State Bank of India vs. P.V. George
issuing_authority: High Court of Kerala
summary: The High Court ruled that a bank owes a high fiduciary duty of care to its customers in digital transactions. If money is siphoned off through electronic or ATM channels without customer culpability, the bank cannot disown liability. The burden rests strictly upon the bank to demonstrate customer negligence with cogent technical proof.
practical_application: Cited in bank notices and court proceedings to refute standard bank rejection letters asserting 'OTP was entered, so we are not responsible'.

title: Punjab National Bank vs. Leader Valves Ltd.
issuing_authority: National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC)
summary: NCDRC held that unauthorized net banking transactions where customer notified the bank promptly constitute deficiency in banking service. The bank was ordered to refund the entire amount along with 9% interest and litigation costs.
practical_application: Provides strong consumer forum backing for filing compensation claims under Consumer Protection Act, 2019 against recalcitrant banks.

practical_application: The essential first step for any online financial fraud victim to halt funds transfer before approaching local police or filing formal bank letters.

Recommends standard protocols for reporting within the 3-day window.
practical_application: Official regulatory reference establishing that fraudulent techniques like screen sharing and search engine manipulation are systemic digital threats recognized by the central bank.

act: Reserve Bank of India - Financial Education Series

title: Comprehensive Modus Operandi of Digital Banking Frauds
issuing_authority: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)

summary: Official RBI analysis of digital financial crimes: (1) SIM Swap: Scammers obtain duplicate SIM cards using forged IDs to intercept OTPs. (2) Remote Access: Deceiving victims into installing AnyDesk/TeamViewer/QuickSupport to gain complete screen control and siphon funds. (3) Fake Customer Care: Inserting fraudulent contact numbers on Google Search and maps. (4) QR Code Scams: Exploiting ignorance that scanning a QR code is ONLY for debiting funds, never for receiving money. (5) Lottery / Task / Fake Job Frauds. Mandates immediate reporting within 3 days under RBI Zero Liability framework.
practical_application: Official proof that techniques like remote screen sharing and fake search engine results are recognized modus operandi, refuting bank claims of customer collusion.

issuing_authority: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)

summary: Step-by-step grievance procedure: (1) Lodge written complaint with the bank branch / nodal officer. (2) If bank rejects or fails to resolve within 30 days, file on https://cms.rbi.org.in. (3) Select grounds: 'Non-reversal of unauthorized electronic transaction' or 'Deficiency in banking service'. (4) The Ombudsman evaluates bank's adherence to Zero Liability Circular RBI/2017-18/15 and Paragraph 12 burden of proof. (5) Award power: Up to ₹30 lakh for financial loss, plus up to ₹1 lakh for loss of time, expenses, and mental agony.
practical_application: The most powerful, free escalation mechanism for ordinary citizens whose bank complaints have been unlawfully closed or rejected.

title: Mandatory Cyber Incident Reporting within 6 Hours and Log Retention
issuing_authority: Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) / MeitY

summary: Mandates: (1) All financial intermediaries, banks, and payment gateways must report cyber security incidents (including unauthorized access to social media, identity theft, financial system compromise) to CERT-In within SIX (6) HOURS of noticing. (2) All system providers must enable and maintain ICT system logs securely within Indian jurisdiction for a rolling period of 180 DAYS to aid criminal investigation.
practical_application: Can be cited against banks and fintech platforms if they fail to preserve server logs or fail to furnish transaction logs to investigating agencies.
